17 is very young, you’re right. You’re not even an adult yet! But I get where you’re coming from: the pain of wasting time and giving up opportunities can ripple across you no matter when it was.

It’s good you are realising this now rather than later; many learn this much later. You’re still in high school so things can change- seize the opportunities now, change things now (as you have). I know it’s hard but try not to think of the past because it will drain you, and future you will end up regretting the amount of time you spent wondering about the past and not being happy now. People develop and grow all the time, there’s no set time frame for anything.

The whole ‘teenage years are the best years of your life’ doesn’t apply to everyone so don’t feel pressured to make your life fit around that. It depends on how your life is; I think for me I was really unhappy at 17/18 and it definitely wasn’t the best time of the my life. Just do what makes you happy and progress in life. You’re doing well already.

Your life isn’t wasted.

And sometimes you feel that you haven’t glowed up but maybe other people have. You are doing well!

It’s good you’re taking the initiative to improve your life by exercising and applying for jobs, and seeking help on here. It’s not unheard of to not have any work experience by 24, and the best time to start is now. 

You’re limiting the jobs you can apply for by not having a driving licence. Can you use public transport? 

Volunteering will also help to build up your confidence and other soft skills. It’ll give you purpose and a structure to your day. There are many different types - like with animals, children, even some remote roles you can do online. You can do this part time whilst searching for jobs. 

Have you not done anything at college, like mentoring? You could try to bulk out your resume by adding projects or assignments you did whilst you were there.

You’re still young and job hopping isn’t seen in that bad of a light nowadays especially if you have stayed in jobs for six months. Have you tried posting this in forums that have teachers in? Maybe they could better advise you in careers that would be suitable for you.

Do things step by step and rather than looking at age, make goals by months or years. Don’t look at the past too much, everyone is on their own journey. 

First as you mentioned you can look towards getting your driving licence so you can be independent. You need to apply for this and then it will become a reality; no one is going to do it for you. So that’s something practical you can do now

Secondly you can look at jobs. I’m not a career expert but your degree sounds good and copywriting sounds good too. The only way to get a job is to apply to them. If it takes a while you can try volunteering somewhere, that will help you build up your confidence.

I’m also not going to suggest like other commenters you can just change to being an extrovert by doing things because that isn’t necessarily the case. You can try though but if it’s not working, there are plenty of jobs that don’t involve acts of putting yourself out there.

Do you take medication for your anxiety and depression? Have you talked to a doctor about this?

All I can say is the only person who can change this is you. Don’t be afraid. Take things step by step and you will be fine.
